overall: The AG found the Hubbardston Board of Selectmen did not violate the Open Meeting Law: no deliberation outside a meeting, and the chair could limit public participation in an open-session discussion. Two non-OML claims were declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated about a complaint against a planning board member between Feb 1 and the Feb 27 meeting, including through town administrator emails.
allegations.key_passage: Because these e-mails did not involve discussion between or among a quorum of the Board, we find no violation with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board violated the law by not letting the complainant speak on his own behalf at the Feb 27 meeting about allegations against him.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, because it is within the chair's discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, the chair did not violate the Open Meeting Law by preventing Mr. Robinson from addressing the Board in open session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair restricted access to public documents, which is a Public Records Law matter outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: This determination concerns only compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, thus we decline to review allegations of violation of any other laws.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair sent a letter without Board authorization.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this claim would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.
